messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — kicking off canary deploy for v2.4.1 in ~5m. Plan is to enable feature-flag `cache-router.new-routing` in small increments. Observability + rollback rules below.

deploy-bot: Deploy job started: deploy-1769999999 · canary · 3 nodes · pinned image v2.4.1-build-202603

simon: Can we start at 2% instead of 5%? last week the cache change spiked tail latencies when we jumped too fast.

jackie: +1 to 2%. proposal: 2% -> 10% (after 15m) -> 40% (after 30m) -> 100% (manual gate). Manual gates at each step.

maya: Updated constraints: rollback triggers = error-rate increase > 1.5pp absolute OR p95 latency increase > 300ms vs baseline. Also abort if anomaly detection raises alert.

jackie: Commands I'll run at start: 
```bash
# enable 2% in canary
redwood ff set cache-router.new-routing --pct 2 --env canary --reason "v2.4.1 canary"
# pin router service to the new build for canary nodes
redwood deploy pin --service router --version v2.4.1-build-202603 --env canary
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: cache-router.new-routing=2% (canary). Pin applied to router (v2.4.1-build-202603).

rohit: I'll run the small eval suite (e2e-cache-check) against canary sessions and watch distribution of cache misses + correctness. ETA 10m.

ops-bot: Observability note: created dashboard slice "canary/cache-router/new-routing" and short-lived alert group: canary-cache-regress (error_rate, p95_latency).

simon: If the canary looks clean at 15m, who approves the 10% bump? maya or jackie?

maya: I'll give the OK for 10% if no alerts and rohit's eval passes. Jackie to run the ff set.

jackie: Will do. Bump command: `redwood ff set cache-router.new-routing --pct 10 --env canary` (manual).

deploy-bot: Canary metrics (15m): error_rate +0.2pp, p95 latency +45ms, eval:e2e-cache-check=PASS. No alerts.

maya: OK to bump to 10% — proceed.

jackie: Bumping to 10% now.

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: cache-router.new-routing=10% (canary).

rohit: Running larger sampling checks now (perf and correctness). I will call out if we see regressions.

ops-bot: Reminder: release notes draft located at https://internal.redwood/release/2.4.1 — call out the cache-router change and the new rollout knobs.

simon: For the 40% step we should also disable KV-prefetch on a subset (flip `cache-router.prefetch=false` for 5% to sanity check interplay). Any objections?

maya: Good idea. Let's flip prefetch=false for 5% at the 10->40 transition, observe 15m. Jackie, can you apply that as a controlled flag?

jackie: Sure. Command: `redwood ff set cache-router.prefetch --pct 5 --env canary` then after observation we can scale.

deploy-bot: At 40% we will not auto-promote to prod — final jump to 100% is manual and requires sign-off from @maya + one eng oncall.

rohit: Heads-up: baseline for p95 latency used for rules is the last 24h median of router-prod p95 (tag: baseline:router-p95-24h).

maya: Decision log: Ramp plan set to 2% -> 10% -> 40% -> 100% (manual). Rollback criteria documented above. Pinning applied to canary; prod pin will be applied only after 40% looks stable.

jackie: If we see any spike, immediate rollback commands: 
```bash
# quick disable
redwood ff set cache-router.new-routing --pct 0 --env canary --reason "rollback: regression"
# unpin if needed
redwood deploy unpin --service router --env canary
```

simon: Leaving a note: if rollback happens, we should trigger a revocation of any staged config and start a small hotfix branch.

maya: Agreed. Jackie — pls post final canary summary in #eng-releases and update release notes with outcome + known issues.

jackie: Will do. Thanks all. (reaction :thumbsup:)

deploy-bot: Canary complete: no regressions detected after 40m. Current canary ff=10% prefetched=false@5% pinned router v2.4.1-build-202603. Awaiting manual gate for 40% -> 100%.
